subject: Canary fallback & auto-revert authorization for SLA (QuantIntel)
messages:
From: Sara Mills <sara@quantintel.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>; procurement@quantintel.ai
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Canary fallback & SLA carveout request for QINT pilot

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo this week — the throughput looked promising. Our procurement and platform teams have one outstanding ask before we sign: QuantIntel requires a documented mitigation plan that guarantees our 99.9% perceived latency SLA during the 6-week pilot. Specifically, we need an ops-level description of how Redwood will handle A/B/canary rollouts when a new model or config causes increased tail latency for a subset of traffic.

Can you provide confirmation that:
- There is an automatic fallback to the previous pinned model/version when latency exceeds a threshold for N minutes,
- A pin/hold mechanism exists so a proven stable version can be immediately reinstated, and
- We can get a temporary SLA exception documented that outlines the thresholds and the rollback timeline for the pilot.

Tom (cc'd) will coordinate procurement. We're trying to get this into our SOW this week. If easier, a short runbook and a completed exemption form will do.

Thanks,
Sara Mills
Director, Platform Engineering
QuantIntel

[Attachment: initial_requirements.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mills <sara@quantintel.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Canary fallback & SLA carveout request for QINT pilot

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. We can support this during the pilot, but need internal approval for a formal SLA carveout that specifies automatic fallback behavior and pinning exceptions.

Summary of what we propose (draft):
- Canary policy: traffic will be ramped to the new model via staged percentages (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%) with health checks at each step.
- Latency guardrail: if p50 or p95 latency for the canary rises above the production baseline by >25% for 5 consecutive minutes, the system will trigger an automatic rollback to the prior pinned model.
- Auto-revert TTL: post-rollback, the system will continue routing to the pinned model for a 15-minute cooldown while we triage; the canary is quarantined until manual re-evaluation.
- Pinning: customers can pin a specific model/version via the API/console; pins take precedence over automated rollouts.
- Monitoring & runbook: we'll provide an ops runbook with exact metrics, alert thresholds, and an on-call playbook (attached).

Can we get internal sign-off on the 25%/5-min threshold and the 15-minute cooldown? If approved, I'll send Sara an exemption form and the runbook for procurement/legal.

Karthik
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Karthik — looks good. A couple of internal constraints I'd add before we commit an authorization to procurement:

- Tighten the rollback trigger to p95 > baseline + 20% OR p99 crossing baseline by any margin for 3 consecutive minutes. This gives us better protection on tail spikes that impact user experience.
- Reduce cooldown to 10 minutes; longer lockouts risk missing a quick safe follow-up patch.
- Allow QuantIntel to request a controlled pin of up to 10% traffic to the older version for testing, but global pins (100%) must come from our ops on-call.
- Runbook note: include explicit escalation to Legal/Security if the revert indicates data handling regressions.

If we approve the above language, I can sign off and Karthik can send the formal SLA carveout doc and exemption form to the customer.

—Laura
VP, Customer Success (Acting)
Redwood Inference

Sara / Karthik — I agree with Laura's tightened triggers. One operational addendum:

- Require automatic creation of a short incident ticket when a rollback occurs (OPS-4721 created automatically) and capture the canary payload ID + latency histograms.
- Require a read-only snapshot of relevant tracing spans for the rollback window to be shared with QuantIntel under an NDA for the pilot period.

I've attached the completed SLA exemption form and the ops runbook draft. Once legal signs the NDA for the snapshot, we can include the data-sharing clause in the SOW.

I'll route the exemption to Procurement and Legal after Karthik confirms the final numeric thresholds (we currently have: p95 > baseline+20% OR p99 > baseline for 3 min; auto-revert TTL = 10m; pin override rules).

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
